newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka parties in show of strength on May Day.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka parties in show of strength on May Day.

text.p: Sri Lanka's political parties staged huge May Day rallies on Thursday in a show of strength after the ruling People's Alliance (PA) swept recent local government polls.

The PA was to mount a massive rally later in the day at the sprawling Town Hall grounds in central Colombo in a show of unity at a time of reports suggest the seven-party coalition was fraught with differences.

Security was tight in the Sri Lankan capital on Thursday. Four years ago to the day, former president Ranasinghe Premadasa was killed by a suicide bomber during the then ruling United National Party's May Day rally.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, are suspected of having carried out the assassination. They have not claimed responsibility for the killing.

The Democratic United National (Lalith) Front (DUNLF), a member of the ruling alliance, has criticised the government for being too slow to fulfil its election promises. It said it will join the PA's rally.
It has criticised the government for so far failing to introduce a new constitution offering substantial devolution to minority Tamils and aimed at ending Sri Lanka's war.
The government has said the new constitution would be presented to parliament before November this year.
In protest against the government, the DUNLF did not contest the March polls, in which the PA won 194 of the 238 local councils at stake. The main opposition United National Party (UNP) won 43.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government, which has a one-vote majority in parliament, relies on the support of coalition members such as DUNLF and other smaller groups to stay in power.

Ministers from Kumaratunga's Sri Lanka Freedom Party, the main constituent in the PA, have accused DUNLF leader Srimani Athulathmudali, herself a minister, of sponsoring an independent group in local polls. Her party has denied the acusation.
The PA, which came to power in 1994 ending 17 years of UNP rule, says it has made considerable achievements.

"During the past 32 months, we have scored great victories not only on the battle fronts in the north and east, but also in every sector of the economy," President Chandrika Kumaratunga said in a May Day message.

"As a result of restoration of stability in the country, foreign investors are coming in and many schemes are now under implementation for the improvement of the economic conditions of workers," she said.
The UNP this year will hold its rally in Hatton, 90 km (56 miles) east of Colombo, in a bid to woo thousands of tea plantation workers in that region.
